papers.title: Rain to Phone: What an open, end-to-end flood monitoring system shows about Thailand's coordination gap
papers.question: Can public flood feeds become a working rain-to-alert chain without waiting for agencies to merge?
papers.evidence: 124 days of alert records; 44 feeds. Median gauge-to-alert lag was 6.7 minutes in 162 matched alerts. A retrospective watchlist reached 84.4% recall at 12.5% precision (pp. 3-5).
papers.limitation: The replay uses the same gauge network as its reference, not an independent flood record. Alert generation is not phone receipt or protective action; only 29 Telegram subscribers were recorded (pp. 3, 5).

papers.title: Nobody owns the haze: An open, end-to-end warning system for Thailand, and its first 110 days

study.label: Thailand; mainland Southeast Asian fire context

papers.question: What can an open haze-warning chain deliver, and where do monitoring coverage and forecast skill still fall short?
papers.evidence: 110 pre-burning-season days; 58,298 scheduled pulls across 23 logged sources. 98.7% were marked successful despite two token-gated feeds skipping without data. Persistence outperformed the corrected forecast (pp. 3-4).
papers.limitation: This is an early-season systems audit, not a multi-year trend or health-impact study. Telegram handoff to one or two chats does not establish population receipt or response (pp. 1, 3, 6).

papers.title: From Gauge to Shelter: Why Thai Smart-City Programmes Stall Between Measurement and Action
papers.question: Which links between measurement, warning and shelter can a provincial operations room assemble from public data?
papers.evidence: An audit of 311 datasets, 2,869 resources and 177 official shelter rows. The official shelter list contained no coordinates; the system records differing precision for subsequently located shelters (pp. 2-5).
papers.limitation: Catalogue absence means not found in the specified searches, not absent everywhere. This is a descriptive audit and feasibility study, not a test of institutional causes or warning outcomes (pp. 1-3).

papers.title: Seeing a War Without Standing in It: What open ships, planes, satellites and markets reveal about the 2026 Gulf conflict, and where they go blind

study.label: Middle East and Gulf; global comparison areas

papers.question: What can ships, aircraft, thermal satellites, markets and regulators reveal from outside a conflict zone?
papers.evidence: Five observation channels, with control ports and explicit coverage checks. Gulf port calls fell to 28% of their earlier rate; only 17.5% of 68,680 vessel positions were under six hours old (pp. 1-4).
papers.limitation: One-event descriptive comparisons do not identify causes. Sparse receivers, stale positions and industrial heat cannot establish absent activity, weapons attribution or human impact (pp. 2, 5-6).

papers.title: The Last Mile Is Institutional: Why Thailand's Smart Cities Stall Between Monitoring and Action, and What One City Built to Cross It

study.label: Nakhon Si Thammarat city and province

papers.question: What can a city control-tower prototype connect, and which institutional links remain outside its authority?
papers.evidence: A participant case combining 216 catalogue datasets, dated provincial station snapshots and an operational audit. Its 47 adapters support source-labelled briefings and human verification (pp. 3-5).
papers.limitation: Two checks 145 minutes apart do not measure warning delay. Hydraulic and camera calibration, official receipt, adoption and public-safety outcomes remain unestablished (pp. 4-6).

papers.title: From Strategic Foresight to Inspectable Decisions: A Provenance-Aware Scenario Console for Thailand's Economic Clusters

study.label: Thailand; national economic clusters and regional analytical overlays

papers.question: How can a scenario console keep source claims, strategic judgments and executable conventions distinguishable?
papers.evidence: A pinned-code audit of eleven economic clusters and four conditional switches. Exhaustive enumeration produces 16 configurations and 176 cluster-state rows: 32 changed, 144 unchanged. A downloadable source supplement reproduces the results.
papers.limitation: A methods preprint draft, not a forecast or policy-impact evaluation. Complete underlying reports were unavailable for independent reading. Scores are judgments; one-step upgrades are conventions. Later statistical discrepancies do not prove original-vintage errors.

papers.title: Four Gaps and One Chain: Where Thailand's Smart-City and Digital-Government Promotion Stops Short of Action
papers.question: Do four common explanations for stalled Thai smart-city promotion survive contact with national data?
papers.evidence: Of 20 environment and safety headline projects in 21 endorsed city records, 15 stop at sensing and 2 name an alert (pp. 4-5). Certified provinces were not detectably more haze-exposed (delta -0.32, CI -0.61 to +0.01) (p. 5).
papers.limitation: Single-coder one-line titles, one-province audits, no outcome series, and authors who built the systems and work for the studied agency; procurement is untestable (pp. 7-8).
